summary: Advance ESG and responsible mining practices with practical frameworks, risk tools, and mine-site strategies. Enroll your team today.
lede: ESG and responsible mining bring environmental, social and governance considerations into each stage of a mine’s life cycle, from exploration to closure. Designed for mining professionals who influence operational and strategic decisions, the course addresses assessing site impacts and integrating ESG into planning. Participants practice materiality assessment, risk-register scoring, stakeholder mapping, and preparing performance dashboards and disclosures.
audienceIntro: This advanced ESG and responsible mining course is tailored for professionals who already influence decisions across the mining life cycle and now need to systematize ESG integration, risk management, and disclosure at a higher standard.
audience: Responsible Sourcing or Supply Chain Manager –
Corporate Affairs or Stakeholder Relations Head –
modules: ESG Foundations in the Mining Life Cycle
Measuring Impacts with Mining ESG Frameworks
Environmental Stewardship, Tailings, and Water Management
Social Performance, Human Rights, and Community Relations
Governance, ESG Risk Registers, and Board Oversight
Digital ESG Data, KPIs, and Performance Dashboards
Stakeholder Engagement, Disclosure, and Reporting for Mining
Integrating ESG into Mine Strategy, Investment, and Closure
prerequisites: This is an advanced-level course designed for experienced mining and ESG professionals. You should have at least 5 years of experience in mining operations, HSE, sustainability, social performance, or related project roles, and a working understanding of basic ESG concepts and mining project phases (exploration, development, operations, closure). Prior exposure to standards such as GRI, ICMM Mining Principles, or IFC Performance Standards is strongly recommended but not mandatory. No coding or advanced statistics are required; however, you should be comfortable working with spreadsheets and digital dashboards for ESG data analysis. Bringing your organization’s existing ESG policies, risk registers, or sustainability reports is encouraged so you can work on real material during exercises.
